SQLite database file managed by packages/storage

Pluggable backend required; no default

New run id with parentRunId pointing to the original
New run id and archive/lock the original run
No true resume; only rerun from scratch with copied config

options.text: Extract an explicit DAG of question ids; validate acyclic; block until deps answered
No dependencies; always a flat list of questions
Infer dependencies implicitly each iteration (no stored graph)

questions.prompt: What budgeting policy should be the default to avoid mid-finalize failures?

options.text: Per-iteration soft cap with a reserved finalize budget; stop between iterations when low
Single global maxRuntimeMs that may stop mid-iteration or mid-finalize
Hard per-iteration wall-clock kill (may interrupt synthesis)
Always finish the current iteration even if it exceeds budget
No runtime budget; only maxIterations

answers.notes: To be clear what I mean by choosing D is that at the end of the current iteration it should then bypass the review and the gap analysis and just synthesize the final writing output into the result. By the time we get there we should already have a very refined result and if we're just out of time, that's fine. Try to do everything we can to land the plane cleanly. I don't want 'Hey we ran out of time, failure modes' but I also don't want this to go on forever, especially on a simple prompt.

questions.prompt: How should synthesis context be managed for iteration N>1 to keep costs flat?

options.text: Carry forward a structured synthesis summary + include only new abstracts/deltas
Carry forward all prior abstracts and the full prior synthesis
Naive truncation: drop oldest tokens until within limits
Only per-question summaries; no global synthesis summary
No compression; rely on model context window

answers.notes: allow full context, but summarize if output budget is < 50,000 tokens. -- make this a feature flag. default A.
